audit_result.proof_trace: `_verifyCanPublishSaleResults()` guards re-entry by checking `totalTokensAllocated != 0`, but `publishSaleResults()` accepts `tokensAllocated = 0` without validation. When called with zero, the sentinel is never set, the guard remains bypassable indefinitely, and merkle roots (`claimTokensMerkleRoot`, `acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot`) can be overwritten on each subsequent call — violating the publish-once invariant.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Legion (legionBouncer) calls `publishSaleResults(maliciousMerkleRoot, maliciousMerkleRoot, 0, 18)`: the guard passes (totalTokensAllocated still 0), fraudulent roots are written, and users who claim against them receive incorrect allocations; Legion can then overwrite again, breaking the immutability guarantee entirely.

PROP-01b-partial-inv-008.text: resultsPublished transitions from false to true exactly once; cannot be reset or overwritten.
